text: In LiteRT-LM agello-next (7b872544), c/engine.h defines LITERT_LM_C_API_VERSION_MAJOR 1, LITERT_LM_C_API_VERSION_MINOR 0 and LITERT_LM_C_API_VERSION_PATCH 0, and version.bzl sets C_API_VERSION = "1.0.0" next to the runtime VERSION = "0.19.0".
In the v0.18.0 tree Agello ships (agello branch 85b1a776), version.bzl sets VERSION = "0.18.0" and C_API_VERSION = "0.2.0".

litert_lm_get_api_version (C API 1.0.0, c/engine.cc) checks that out_major, out_minor and out_patch are all non-NULL before writing any, then writes the LITERT_LM_C_API_VERSION_* values the library was compiled with; the c/engine.h comment tells dynamic loaders to compare them with the header macros and to treat a library that doesn't export the function (older than 1.0.0) as incompatible.

c/error_reporter.h (C API 1.0.0) states: every function that can fail returns a LiteRtLmStatusCode (kLiteRtLmStatusOk = 0, positive on failure); results come through trailing out_* parameters; a NULL out-parameter yields kLiteRtLmStatusInvalidArgument; pointer out-parameters are set to NULL on failure and scalar ones are left untouched; a legitimately absent value is a success that writes NULL; only the NULL-safe *_delete destructors and the error-reporter functions return no status.

LiteRtLmStatusCode (c/error_reporter.h) has 17 enumerators, kLiteRtLmStatusOk = 0 through kLiteRtLmStatusUnauthenticated = 16, numerically identical to absl::StatusCode / google.rpc.Code and documented as frozen; callers should treat unknown values as kLiteRtLmStatusUnknown. The same enum exists in the v0.18.0 header (added in 0.2.0).
ToLiteRtLmStatusCode in c/error_reporter.cc maps any absl::StatusCode value outside 0..16 to kLiteRtLmStatusUnknown and casts the others unchanged.

In c/error_reporter.cc the last error message is a per-thread std::string (static thread_local); it is written only when a call fails and is not cleared by successful calls; litert_lm_get_last_error_message returns NULL when the string is empty; litert_lm_clear_last_error swaps the string with an empty one to release its buffer.

In the C API's error helpers (c/error_reporter.cc), a failure converted from an absl::Status (ToCStatus) records status.ToString() as the last error message, while ReturnError and the LITERT_LM_C_RETURN_IF_NULL macro record only their message text (for example "<arg> must not be NULL.").

c/engine.h (C API 1.0.0) states that LiteRT-LM C handles are not reference counted or reparented, that every session and conversation must be destroyed before the engine that created it, and that destroying an engine with live children or using a child after its engine is destroyed is undefined behavior.

In c/engine_internal.h, LiteRtLmEngineSettings wraps std::unique_ptr<litert::lm::EngineSettings>, LiteRtLmEngine wraps std::unique_ptr<litert::lm::Engine>, and LiteRtLmSession wraps std::unique_ptr<litert::lm::Engine::Session>.

litert_lm_input_data_create (c/engine.cc) copies the given bytes into a std::string for text, image and audio inputs (image-end and audio-end carry no data), and ToEngineInputData copies each input again for session calls while skipping NULL entries in the input array.

litert_lm_engine_settings_create (c/engine.cc) parses backend strings with GetBackendFromString, which accepts cpu, gpu, npu, gpu_artisan, cpu_artisan and google_tensor_artisan case-insensitively and returns InvalidArgument otherwise; a NULL main backend string becomes an empty string (absl::NullSafeStringView) and fails, while a NULL or empty vision or audio backend string leaves that executor unconfigured.

litert_lm_engine_settings_create_from_raw_file_descriptor (c/engine.cc) rejects a negative fd with InvalidArgument and otherwise wraps the fd in a ScopedFile inside the model assets (the header says the engine takes ownership and closes it).

In c/engine.cc, litert_lm_engine_settings_set_num_threads edits the main executor's CpuConfig and litert_lm_engine_settings_set_gpu_decode_steps_per_sync edits GpuArtisanConfig; when the main backend config is of another type they change nothing and still return kLiteRtLmStatusOk (set_num_threads logs a warning).

litert_lm_engine_settings_set_gpu_enable_metal_residency_set (c/engine.cc) writes AdvancedSettings::gpu_enable_metal_residency_set, whose default is false (runtime/executor/llm_executor_settings.h); its header comment says it only acts on Apple platforms with the GPU backend (MTLResidencySet) and is ignored elsewhere; litert_lm_experimental_engine_update_gpu_enable_metal_residency_set changes it on a live engine through Engine::UpdateGpuEnableMetalResidencySet.
litert_lm_engine_create (c/engine.cc) creates the engine with EngineFactory::CreateDefault(*settings->settings) and stores it in a new LiteRtLmEngine; the settings handle stays owned by the caller.

Both litert_lm_engine_create_session (c/engine.cc) and litert_lm_conversation_create (c/conversation.cc) call SetAudioModalityEnabled(true) / SetVisionModalityEnabled(true) on the session config whenever the engine's settings have audio / vision executor settings.

litert_lm_sampler_params_create (c/engine.cc) initializes top_k, top_p, temperature and seed to 0, and litert_lm_session_config_set_sampler_params copies type, k, p, temperature and seed into the session config's SamplerParameters proto.

litert_lm_conversation_create (c/conversation.cc) wraps the configured system message in a {"role": "system"} message, using the parsed JSON as content, or the raw text as a string when it is not valid JSON.

litert_lm_conversation_create (c/conversation.cc) only logs (ABSL_LOG(ERROR)) and ignores initial messages that are not a valid JSON array and tools JSON that is not a valid array, and the conversation is still created.

In litert_lm_conversation_create (c/conversation.cc), a constraint provider of kLiteRtLmConstraintProviderTypeLlGuidance sets the builder's constraint provider to LlGuidanceConfig(), and rewinding is disabled only when the main executor uses GpuArtisanConfig with use_autosized_ringbuffers.
litert_lm_conversation_create (c/conversation.cc) uses ConversationConfig::CreateDefault(engine) when the config argument is NULL.

The ConversationConfig builder (runtime/conversation/conversation.h) defaults to enable_constrained_decoding false, filter_channel_content_from_kv_cache true, stream_tool_calls false with channel name "tool_call", and enable_rewinding true.

litert_lm_conversation_send_message (c/conversation.cc) is blocking: it rejects unparsable message JSON with InvalidArgument, calls Conversation::SendMessage, and returns the reply as Message::dump() in a LiteRtLmJsonResponse.

For litert_lm_conversation_send_message_stream (c/conversation.cc), each non-final chunk's text is the JSON dump of a partial Message; an empty Message becomes a final chunk with no text and no error; a non-OK status becomes a final chunk with no text and error = status.ToString(). v0.18.0's c/conversation.cc has the same callback.

For the session streaming calls (litert_lm_session_run_decode_async, litert_lm_session_generate_content_stream), CreateCallback in c/engine.cc sends one non-final chunk per candidate text, a final chunk without error on kDone, a final chunk with error "Max number of tokens reached." on kMaxNumTokensReached, a final chunk with error "CANCELLED." on kCancelled, and a final chunk with status.ToString() on errors.

A LiteRtLmStreamChunk (c/engine.h) is owned by the library and valid only during the callback; the C layer builds it on the stack around temporary std::string values (c/conversation.cc CreateConversationCallback), so text and error pointers read from it must be copied before the callback returns.

With single-threaded execution off (EngineSettings default false), the engine uses ThreadedExecutionManager, which creates an execution thread pool and a callback thread pool of one thread each; decode tasks call Tasks::Decode with the stream callback on the execution thread, the final callback is scheduled on the callback thread, and the execution thread then waits up to 10 seconds (WaitUntilDone(absl::Seconds(10))) for the callback pool.

c/conversation.h (C API 1.0.0) says litert_lm_conversation_wait_until_done must be called after litert_lm_conversation_send_message_stream when the engine uses single-threaded execution, because queued work only progresses while a caller drives it and the stream callback is invoked from inside that call.

litert_lm_conversation_cancel_process calls Conversation::CancelProcess, which calls the session's CancelProcess (cancel all tasks of the session); runtime/core/session_advanced.h notes, in both agello-next and v0.18.0, that reusing a session after CancelProcess is neither recommended nor supported because it leaves the session state poisoned.

In c/conversation.cc, setting a repetition penalty config that is NULL or not enabled() clears it from the optional args; CreateOptionalArgs maps kLiteRtLmConstraintTypeRegex / kLiteRtLmConstraintTypeJsonSchema to an LlGuidanceConstraintArg of kRegex / kJsonSchema, and passes the visual token budget only as Gemma4DataProcessorArguments when the session's model type is Gemma 4.
litert_lm_thinking_config_create (c/conversation.cc) creates ThinkingConfig(true, -1): thinking enabled with an unlimited budget.

litert_lm_conversation_render_message_to_string stores its result in the LiteRtLmConversation's last_rendered_message string and returns a pointer into it, so the string stays valid until the next such call or the conversation's deletion.

litert_lm_conversation_get_token_count reports the tokens in the conversation's KV cache (prefill plus decode): in C API 1.0.0 as a status with the count in out_count, in v0.18.0's C API 0.2 as an int return that is negative on failure.

The C headers of LiteRT-LM agello-next 7b872544 declare 220 functions: engine.h 111, conversation.h 39, embedding_engine.h 34, model_info.h 21, experimental.h 6, error_reporter.h 2, and our telemetry.h 6 and build_info.h 1.

text: Google's prebuilt v0.18.0 CLiteRTLM iOS arm64 binary exports 212 litert_lm_* C functions and our agello-next binary 220; only Google's exports litert_lm_get_last_error_code, and only ours exports litert_lm_conversation_wait_until_done, litert_lm_get_api_version, litert_lm_get_build_info and six litert_lm_telemetry_* functions.

sources.detail: row 'Exported litert_lm_* C functions' (212 vs 220) and section 'C functions exported by one binary only'

text: In C API 0.2.0 (v0.18.0, agello 85b1a776), litert_lm_engine_create returns LiteRtLmEngine* (NULL on failure), litert_lm_conversation_send_message_stream returns int (0 on success; -1 for invalid arguments, otherwise the absl status code), litert_lm_conversation_get_token_count returns an int that is negative on failure, and the error code is read with int litert_lm_get_last_error_code(void).

c/conversation.h at agello-next annotates litert_lm_conversation_wait_until_done 'Added in version 0.2.0', but the v0.18.0 tree (C API 0.2.0) doesn't declare it and Google's v0.18.0 binary doesn't export it.

Our C additions don't use LiteRtLmStatusCode: c/telemetry.h declares void litert_lm_telemetry_set_level(int), int _get_level(void), char* _snapshot_json(void) (malloc'd, freed with litert_lm_telemetry_free_string), void _reset(void) and bool _write_trace(const char*); c/build_info.h declares const char* litert_lm_get_build_info(void) returning static storage.

Agello telemetry (ours, agello/telemetry/agello/agello_telemetry.cc) starts at level 1 (counters) unless the AGELLO_TELEMETRY environment variable is set, in which case its integer value clamped to 0..4 is used; when AGELLO_TELEMETRY_OUT is set, the snapshot JSON is written to that path at process exit, and the trace to <path>.trace.json at level 3 or more.

litert_lm_get_build_info (ours) returns a JSON object with string fields build_id, litert_lm, litert, ml_drift and flags, generated by agello/make_build_info.sh from Bazel's stable-status values (STABLE_AGELLO_*) that agello/workspace_status.sh prints under --config=agello; missing values default to "dev" for build_id and "unknown" for the others.
litert_lm_experimental_is_debugger_enabled (c/experimental.cc) reports whether the library was compiled with LITERT_LM_DEBUGGER_ENABLED defined; it is a compile-time setting.

c/model_info.h documents litert_lm_loaded_file_max_context_tokens as the fixed context size for static models, the largest settable size for dynamic ones, and kLiteRtLmStatusNotFound when the model doesn't define it (C API 1.0.0).

The C++ EmbeddingOptions defaults (runtime/engine/embedding_engine.h) are normalize = true, insert_special_tokens = true, input_overflow_strategy = kError, and no vision-token or output-size override; the C enum LiteRtLmInputOverflowStrategy offers chunk-and-average, truncate and error.
litert_lm_embedding_responses_get_at returns a response borrowed from the LiteRtLmEmbeddingResponses batch, valid until the batch is deleted and not to be deleted by the caller.

Under #if defined(__APPLE__), the LiteRT-LM C headers include each other by bare file name ("api_export.h", "error_reporter.h") instead of "c/..." paths, and LITERT_LM_C_API_EXPORT is __attribute__((visibility("default"))) on non-Windows platforms unless the client predefines it.
In runtime/executor/executor_settings_base.cc, a cache directory of ":nocache" disables the weight cache.

SessionAdvanced's destructor calls WaitUntilDone(), which waits up to Engine::kDefaultTimeout (absl::Minutes(10)) for the session's tasks without cancelling them, in both agello-next and v0.18.0; the wait (ThreadedExecutionManager::WaitUntilSessionDone) ends when the session has no active task, and tasks leave that state only in an end state (done, max tokens, failed, cancelled).

When a conversation's task is cancelled, runtime/conversation/internal_callback_util.cc calls the user callback with absl::CancelledError("Task cancelled"), and the C stream callback turns it into a final chunk whose error is status.ToString(), i.e. "CANCELLED: Task cancelled".
LiteRT-LM v0.18.0's ThreadedExecutionManager also creates execution and callback thread pools of one thread each and waits up to 10 seconds for the callback pool after scheduling the final callback.

In the LiteRTLM Swift package, Engine is an actor whose initialize() is a synchronous actor-isolated method that runs the whole native engine creation (blocking the actor and its thread) and throws LiteRTLMError.engine(.alreadyInitialized) if called again.

Engine.initialize (swift/Engine.swift, agello-next) creates settings with litert_lm_engine_settings_create from EngineConfig.backend.rawValue and the optional vision/audio backends, applies the setters, creates the engine with litert_lm_engine_create, and deletes the settings with defer.

Backend.cpu(threadCount:) in swift/Config.swift carries a thread count, but Engine.initialize never calls litert_lm_engine_settings_set_num_threads (its setter calls are maxNumTokens, cacheDir, activation type, LoRA ranks, benchmark and the experimental flags), so the count is ignored for LLM engines; EmbeddingEngine.initialize does apply it when positive.

Engine.initialize (agello-next) reads the process-wide ExperimentalFlags enableBenchmark, enableSpeculativeDecoding, visualTokenBudget (passed to litert_lm_engine_settings_set_max_vision_tokens_per_image), gpuEnableMetalResidencySet and enableYnnpack, and passes each to its C setter only when set (enableBenchmark when true).

Engine.deinit deletes the native engine with litert_lm_engine_delete, and each Conversation stores a strong reference to the Engine that created it, so a Swift engine is not deinitialized while any of its conversations is alive.
Engine.createConversation throws LiteRTLMError.config(.multipleSystemMessages) when ConversationConfig has both a systemMessage and an initial system message, or more than one initial system message.

When ConversationConfig.samplerConfig is set, Engine.createConversation always creates C sampler params of type kLiteRtLmSamplerTypeTopP and sets top-k, top-p, temperature and seed from it; with no samplerConfig it sets no sampler params.

In Engine.createConversation, enableResponseFormat = true sets the llguidance constraint provider and enables constrained decoding; otherwise constrained decoding is set from ExperimentalFlags.enableConversationConstrainedDecoding (default false); tool-call streaming is enabled only if both ConversationConfig.enableToolCallStreaming and ExperimentalFlags.enableConversationToolCallStreaming are true, with ExperimentalFlags.conversationToolCallStreamingChannelName as the channel.

Engine.createConversation passes ExperimentalFlags.filterChannelContentFromKvCache to the C config only when it is non-nil; the C++ ConversationConfig builder's default for filter_channel_content_from_kv_cache is true.

Conversation (swift/Conversation.swift) is a final class declared Sendable whose stored properties are all let constants (handle, toolManager, automaticToolCalling, engine, enableResponseFormat, visualTokenBudget), with no lock or actor isolation; its deinit calls litert_lm_conversation_delete.
Conversation.sendMessage is declared async but calls the blocking C function litert_lm_conversation_send_message synchronously, so it occupies the calling thread for the whole reply.

Conversation.sendMessage runs an automatic tool loop of at most recurringToolCallLimit = 25 rounds: it returns the reply when it has no tool_calls or when automaticToolCalling is false, otherwise runs the tools and sends their responses; the thinking config is passed only on the first round; after 25 rounds it throws conversation(.recurringToolCallLimitExceeded(limit: 25)).

Conversation.sendMessageStream returns an AsyncThrowingStream whose build closure starts the native stream immediately and registers no onTermination handler (no onTermination appears in the Swift sources), so cancelling the consuming task or dropping the stream does not stop native generation; only Conversation.cancel() does.

Conversation.sendToStream retains a StreamContext with Unmanaged.passRetained, passes it as callback_data to litert_lm_conversation_send_message_stream with streamCallback, and when the call doesn't return kLiteRtLmStatusOk releases the context and throws conversation(.failedToStartStream(status:message:)).

The Swift streamCallback is the C stream callback, so with the default threaded execution manager it runs on LiteRT-LM's execution thread for partial chunks (Tasks::Decode receives the callback) and on its callback thread for the final chunk.

In streamCallback (swift/Conversation.swift), a chunk with an error finishes the stream throwing conversation(.invalidResponse(<error text>)) and releases the context; chunk text is parsed as JSON, any tool_calls are appended to the context's pendingToolCalls, and only chunks with content or channels are yielded as Message values.

On the final stream chunk with pending tool calls (fewer than 25 rounds so far), streamCallback starts a Swift Task that runs the tools and sends the tool responses with a newly retained context; this path never checks automaticToolCalling (StreamContext has no such field), so streamed replies run registered tools even when ConversationConfig.automaticToolCalling is false.

The tool-response follow-up send in streamCallback passes the stream's repetition penalty, no-repeat n-gram, suppressed tokens, maxOutputTokens and responseFormat, but not its extraContext or thinkingConfig.

Upstream's StreamContext (swift/Conversation.swift at upstream base df6df5b8) holds 'let conversation: Conversation'; our patch makes it 'weak var conversation: Conversation?' (commit 0b2ca12fc4 on agello-next, 85b1a77695 in the shipped wrapper).

With a strong StreamContext reference, the release at the end of the final stream callback could drop the last reference to a Conversation the app had already released; Conversation.deinit then ran litert_lm_conversation_delete on the callback thread, the session destructor waited (up to Engine::kDefaultTimeout, 10 minutes) for the session's tasks, and the running task is only marked finished after its final callback returns, so the wait could only end at the timeout.

With our weak StreamContext.conversation, a stream whose conversation was released before a tool round finishes with conversation(.notAlive) in the follow-up Task, and the conversation is deleted on the thread that drops it, where the deletion waits for the stream's work.

Conversation.cancel() calls litert_lm_conversation_cancel_process; a cancelled stream then receives a final chunk whose error text is "CANCELLED: Task cancelled", which streamCallback throws as conversation(.invalidResponse(...)); the wrapper has no separate cancellation error, and upstream documents that a session is not reusable after CancelProcess.

Our handleToolCalls patch (f3408e0671 on agello-next, a3c0d0ef72 shipped) answers every tool call: missing or null arguments run the tool with {}, an object or a JSON string holding an object runs it, other argument values get {"error": "The arguments for '<name>' must be a JSON object."}, tool(.notFound) gets "There is no tool named '<name>'. Use only the tools you were given, or answer without one.", a DecodingError gets "The arguments for '<name>' don't match its parameters. Check their names and types, then try again.", and any other thrown error gets "'<name>' failed: <localizedDescription>".

Upstream's handleToolCalls (base df6df5b8) skipped calls whose arguments were not a JSON object and rethrew any tool error as LiteRTLMError.conversation(.toolExecutionError(name:error:)), ending the reply; after our patch the toolExecutionError case still exists in LiteRTLMError but nothing in the package throws it.

A LiteRTLM Tool is a Decodable type with static name and description, an empty init() and run() async throws -> Any; @ToolParam(description:) parameters may be String, Int, Bool, Double or Float (JSON number), an Optional of these (schema nullable: true), or an Array of these.
A @ToolParam parameter is required unless its type is Optional or it has a default value, and reading the wrappedValue of a required parameter that was never set calls fatalError.

Tool.getSchema() emits {"type": "function", "function": {name, description, parameters}} with an object schema of the @ToolParam properties (and a required list); when ExperimentalFlags.convertCamelToSnakeCaseInToolDescription is true (the default) tool and parameter names are converted from camelCase to snake_case after dropping the property wrapper's leading underscore.

ToolManager.execute reads ExperimentalFlags.convertCamelToSnakeCaseInToolDescription again on every call (for the default-value keys and the JSONDecoder key strategy), while the tool registry names are fixed in ToolManager.init at conversation creation; the flag's documentation says it is read only when a new Conversation is created.
conflicts_with: swift/ExperimentalFlags.swift doc comment: 'This flag is read only when a new [Conversation] is created.'

text: ToolManager.execute merges the model's arguments over defaults read from a fresh tool instance (null for optional parameters without a default), decodes a new tool instance with JSONDecoder, runs it, and normalizes the result: dictionaries and arrays recursively, String/Int/Double/Float/Bool unchanged, Void as "", anything else via String(describing:).

ResponseFormat.json(schema:) accepts a JSON string (checked to parse) or a dictionary and maps to kLiteRtLmConstraintTypeJsonSchema; ResponseFormat.regex(pattern:) maps to kLiteRtLmConstraintTypeRegex; sendMessage and sendMessageStream throw conversation(.responseFormatNotEnabled) when given a format on a conversation created without enableResponseFormat.

Conversation.shouldApplyResponseFormat skips the response format for a message when automatic tool calling is on, the conversation has tools (toolsJsonDescription is not "[]"), and the message's role is not "tool"; tool-response messages and conversations without tools get the format.

ExperimentalFlags is a struct of static var flags (process-wide, unsynchronized); each setter ignores the new value and logs an error unless optIntoExperimentalAPIs() was called, and optedIn has no public way to be reset.

ExperimentalFlags.visualTokenBudget is read by Engine.initialize (as the engine's max vision tokens per image) and again for every message by makeOptionalArgs, which uses ConversationConfig.visualTokenBudget or, when that is nil, the flag's current value.

ExperimentalFlags.enableYnnpack exists only in agello-next: when unset, its getter returns true if the environment variable ENABLE_YNNPACK or enable_ynnpack equals "true" or a process argument contains "enable_ynnpack=true" (no opt-in needed); the shipped wrapper's ExperimentalFlags ends with gpuEnableMetalResidencySet and has no such flag.

The benchmark(...) function in swift/Benchmark.swift calls ExperimentalFlags.optIntoExperimentalAPIs() and sets ExperimentalFlags.enableBenchmark to true for its duration, restoring the previous value with defer.
LiteRTLMError has seven top-level cases: engine, embeddingEngine, conversation, config, tool, message and modelInfo, each wrapping a nested error enum.

In agello-next, LiteRTLMError.check turns a non-OK LiteRtLmStatusCode into the caller's error with the text "<function> failed with status <code>: <message>", where the message comes from consumeLastError, which reads and then clears the C thread-local last error; create additionally throws when the returned handle is NULL.
LiteRTLMError.EngineError's == treats two errors of the same case with detail strings as equal when the strings match or either is empty.
The shipped wrapper (85b1a776) has LiteRTLMError.getLastErrorCode() calling litert_lm_get_last_error_code(), a C function of C API 0.2; agello-next's wrapper has no getLastErrorCode.

ModelInfo's accessors don't throw: modelInfoValue returns a fallback when the C call fails or reports NotFound (for example maxContextTokens() returns 0), and fetchIntArray returns nil when the count query fails.

EmbeddingEngine is an actor; initialize() applies Backend.cpu(threadCount:) through litert_lm_embedding_engine_settings_set_num_threads when the count is positive, and close() and deinit delete the native embedding engine.

Swift EmbeddingOptions exposes normalize, insertSpecialTokens, outputSize and visionTokensPerImage but no input overflow strategy, so Swift embedding calls use the C++ default input_overflow_strategy = kError (an input longer than the longest signature fails).
BuildInfo (ours, swift/BuildInfo.swift, agello-next only) returns litert_lm_get_build_info() as json, decodes it as [String: String] in fields, and exposes fields["build_id"] as id.

Telemetry (ours, swift/Telemetry.swift, agello-next only) has Level off = 0, counters = 1, spans = 2, trace = 3, deep = 4, a level property over litert_lm_telemetry_get_level/set_level, snapshotJSON() (frees the C string with litert_lm_telemetry_free_string), snapshot(), reset() and writeTrace(to:).

The shipped Package.swift (85b1a776) pins Google's v0.18.0 CLiteRTLM.xcframework.zip (iOS) and CLiteRTLM_mac.xcframework.zip (macOS) by release URL and checksum and picks them by platform condition, while agello-next's Package.swift has one binaryTarget CLiteRTLM at the local path dist/CLiteRTLM.xcframework (ours, 3b2327cfcd).

Agello at commit 93122b647a vendors the shipped wrapper unchanged: Vendor/LiteRT-LM/Package.swift and every file under Vendor/LiteRT-LM/swift/ are byte-identical to the corresponding files of PowerBeef/agello-litert-lm at 85b1a776.
Both the shipped and agello-next Package.swift declare swift-tools-version 5.9 and platforms iOS 15 and macOS 12.

The shipped Engine.swift calls litert_lm_engine_settings_create with four arguments and tests the returned pointer (C API 0.2), while the C API 1.0.0 function takes a fifth out-parameter and returns a LiteRtLmStatusCode, so each wrapper only compiles against its own headers.

The apple_fm adapter (LiteRTLMFoundationModels) compiles only under '#if canImport(FoundationModels) && compiler(>=6.4)', makes LiteRTLanguageModel available from iOS 27 / macOS 27, builds a new LiteRT Conversation from the whole Foundation Models transcript on every respond call, and shares one Engine per configuration through a process-wide EngineCache.

When generated/swift-api-inventory.md was built at agello-next 7b872544 with swift package dump-symbol-graph, the LiteRTLMFoundationModels target (swift/apple_fm) did not compile against the macOS 27 SDK, so only the LiteRTLM module is listed.

text: In swift/Message.swift, Role raw values are system, user, assistant (case .model) and tool, and Content serializes as {type: text, text}, {type: image, blob (base64) or path}, {type: audio, blob or path} and {type: tool_response, name, response, optional id}.
Conversation.jsonToMessage maps role "assistant" or "model" to Role.model and throws message(.invalidContent) when the JSON has no content, channels or tool calls.

EngineConfig throws config(.invalidMaxNumTokens) for maxNumTokens <= 0; SamplerConfig throws for topK <= 0, topP outside [0, 1] or temperature < 0; ThinkingConfig() defaults to enableThinking true and thinkingTokenBudget -1 (unlimited).
ConversationConfig.init drops a system message whose text is empty and re-creates a system message given with another role as Role.system.

Engine.updateGPUEnableMetalResidencySet(_:) throws engine(.notOptedIntoExperimentalAPIs) unless ExperimentalFlags.optedIn, then calls litert_lm_experimental_engine_update_gpu_enable_metal_residency_set.

Agello's LiteRTChatEngine.load (93122b647a) calls ExperimentalFlags.optIntoExperimentalAPIs(), sets enableBenchmark = true and filterChannelContentFromKvCache = true, and sets ExperimentalFlags.enableSpeculativeDecoding from its plan before creating engines.

Agello's makeEngine builds EngineConfig with backend .gpu or .cpu(), vision and audio backends .cpu() when enabled, maxNumTokens from its plan and a cache directory per context size, and awaits engine.initialize() inside Task.detached.

Agello validates each new engine by sending "Hi" with maxOutputTokens 1 on a throwaway conversation, because (per its comment) LiteRT-LM can report a successful load when part of the model failed to map.

Agello's JSON helper conversations use ConversationConfig(enableResponseFormat: true, enableSpeculativeDecoding: false) and sendMessage with responseFormat .json(schema:); its comment says MTP-drafted tokens bypassed the JSON mask on device.

Agello streams replies with sendMessageStream(_:maxOutputTokens:), checks Task.isCancelled on every chunk and calls conversation.cancel() when cancelled or when output would overflow the room left in the KV cache, and treats a cancelled conversation as unusable (reseeding before the next send).
Agello's LiteRTEmbedder uses EmbeddingEngine with EmbeddingOptions(normalize: true, outputSize: 256), embeds documents in computeEmbeddingBatch calls of 8, and initializes on .gpu first, then .cpu().

Agello's chat conversation registers CurrentDateTimeTool and CalculatorTool when tools are enabled, plus WebSearchTool when web search is automatic, with a SamplerConfig, a ThinkingConfig built from its thinking budget, its visual token budget and per-conversation speculative decoding.
Agello's unload sets its Conversation to nil before its Engine, so the native conversation is deleted before the engine.

Between the shipped wrapper (85b1a776) and agello-next (7b872544), the lines declaring public API in swift/Engine.swift, swift/Conversation.swift, swift/EmbeddingEngine.swift and swift/ModelInfo.swift are identical; agello-next's port of these files to C API 1.0.0 (LiteRTLMError.check/create/get) comes from Google's upstream base df6df5b8, since our commits change only swift/Conversation.swift, swift/BUILD, swift/BuildInfo.swift and swift/Telemetry.swift.
